second_order: starting Frank marks with calls and coordinates
theme_note: These codes hold together as attempts to begin a visible Frank Ocean or Frankie mark: posters call, choose a target or coordinates, and one person joins. What varies is the proposed wording or picture and whether the participant is calling, locating, or joining.

second_order: calling out how the drawing looks
theme_note: This code evaluates the visible attempt by criticizing the letter being drawn; it belongs with no other practice yet and remains a legitimate single-code theme.

second_order: fooling and checking one another on April Fools
theme_note: These codes are the room doing its own April Fools conduct rather than canvas work: people post or anticipate fake album, radio, and appearance news, identify the trick, admit believing it, and rebuke it while laughing. What varies is whether a turn makes, warns against, falls for, or corrects the joke.

These codes hold together as participants turning possible art into coordinated work: they assess whether enough people exist, propose a design, choose corners and borders, resize or relocate, schedule participation, sequence construction, open a chat, direct lettering, and ask what to do next. What varies is the target and the particular coordination problem being solved.

second_order: making truces and asking other groups for help
theme_note: These codes are outward-facing coordination: participants describe an invasion, seek a truce, pair with NASCAR, propose merging or touching borders, and recruit Kanye, indieheads, or HHH. What varies is whether the other group is treated as a threat, neighbour, ally, or source of placing power.

second_order: celebrating a finished build and turning to defense
theme_note: These codes form an explicit transition: the room congratulates itself for completing Channel Orange, asks what comes next, and answers that completion now requires defense.

second_order: showing the cult power on the canvas
theme_note: These codes use the cult-not-clique identity of the room as both a rallying claim and material for the design. What varies is whether participants name the mission, put the line into pixels, or propose the next identity-bearing addition.

second_order: explaining the pixel posts and the room builds
theme_note: These codes answer people who do not understand the pixel images or mechanics by naming r/place, explaining the timer, and recounting what the subreddit built. The common practice is bringing late or confused readers into the shared account.

second_order: reacting to what appears on r/place
theme_note: This single code records a participant reacting to an event image without a more specific surviving description; it belongs with no other practice in the pool at this point.

These codes are the practical work of keeping existing marks legible: participants clean borders, answer vandalism or attack reports, call defenders, repair damage, and prefer protection over further expansion. What varies is the design under pressure and whether the response is a call, instruction, reassurance, or repair.

second_order: arguing about whether r/place belongs in the room
theme_note: These codes dispute the place of event talk itself: one person calls the event lame, another defends letting people enjoy it, and a poster tries to move place discussion to a new subreddit. The variation is between rejection, defense of enjoyment, and attempted redirection.

second_order: closing the event and recounting what remained
theme_note: This code withdraws a redesign because place has ended. It opens a post-event practice that later slices may extend with recounting, mourning, and memorializing.

These codes turn the destruction dispute into curses, slogans, mockery, proposed meme raids, search manipulation, and reminders aimed at Denmark. What varies is whether the grievance is voiced as anger, a room joke, a threat of retaliation, or a proposed new placement.
This code is a Danish apology for destructive placing. It begins a distinct post-event practice of apology and possible reconciliation that later replies may extend.

These codes move the shared build to successor canvases after the original closes, recruiting painters and trying to reactivate the subreddit. The practice is continuation elsewhere rather than recollection alone.
